theory.intro: For square-root surds with positive integer radicands, a surd is in **simplest form** when no square factor greater than $1$ remains under the root. Once simplified, surds behave like pronumerals: $5\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{3}=3\sqrt{3}$ works just like $5x-2x=3x$.
facts: To simplify a surd, split off the **highest square factor** of the number under the root: $\sqrt{72}=\sqrt{36}\times\sqrt{2}=6\sqrt{2}$.
Only **like surds** — those with the same number under the root — can be added or subtracted: $4\sqrt{5}+3\sqrt{5}=7\sqrt{5}$, but $4\sqrt{5}+3\sqrt{2}$ cannot.
To multiply, multiply the numbers in front and the numbers under the roots separately: $a\sqrt{x}\times b\sqrt{y}=ab\sqrt{xy}$, for real numbers $a$ and $b$, with $x\geq0$ and $y\geq0$.

To divide, divide the numbers in front and the numbers under the roots separately: $a\sqrt{x}\div b\sqrt{y}=\dfrac{a}{b}\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{y}}$, for real numbers $a$ and $b$, with $x\geq0$, $y>0$ and $b\neq0$.
Always check the final surd: $2\sqrt{50}$ is not finished, because $\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt{2}$ gives $10\sqrt{2}$.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The highest square factor of $63$ is $9$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4\sqrt{63}\\&=4\sqrt{9}\times\sqrt{7}\\&=4\times3\sqrt{7}\\&=12\sqrt{7}\end{aligned}$

Collect like surds; leave the unlike surd separate.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}8\sqrt{7}+3\sqrt{2}-5\sqrt{7}\\&=(8-5)\sqrt{7}+3\sqrt{2}\\&=3\sqrt{7}+3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}$

Simplify each surd, then collect like surds.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3\sqrt{48}-2\sqrt{75}+\sqrt{12}\\&=3\times4\sqrt{3}-2\times5\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{3}\\&=12\sqrt{3}-10\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{3}\\&=4\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$

Multiply the coefficients and radicands separately, then simplify.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4\sqrt{6}\times3\sqrt{10}\\&=12\sqrt{60}\\&=12\sqrt{4}\times\sqrt{15}\\&=24\sqrt{15}\end{aligned}$

Divide the coefficients and radicands separately.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{14\sqrt{108}}{7\sqrt{3}}\\&=2\sqrt{\dfrac{108}{3}}\\&=2\sqrt{36}\\&=12\end{aligned}$

Simplify the surds, then use a common denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{\sqrt{75}}{4}-\dfrac{\sqrt{12}}{3}\\&=\dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{4}-\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\\&=\dfrac{15\sqrt{3}-8\sqrt{3}}{12}\\&=\dfrac{7\sqrt{3}}{12}\end{aligned}$

Simplify and subtract the surds.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{147}-\sqrt{75}\\&=7\sqrt{3}-5\sqrt{3}\\&=2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$
Write the result as one square root.
$\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3}&=\sqrt{4}\times\sqrt{3}\\&=\sqrt{12}\end{aligned}$
Therefore, $x=12$.
